• Fever: It does not come under major Jones criteria for rheumatic fever, but it is a part of Jones minor criteria. Acute rheumatic fever (ARF) is an autoimmune inflammatory process that develops as a sequel of streptococcal infection. Diagnosis of rheumatic fever is made through Jones criteria, which has major and minor criteria.
  • Revised Jones criteria, low-risk populations: Major and minor criteria are as follows:
    • Major criteria: Carditis (clinical and/or subclinical), arthritis (polyarthritis), chorea, erythema marginatum, and subcutaneous nodules.
    • Minor criteria: Polyarthralgia, fever (≥ 38.5° F), sedimentation rate ≥ 60 mm and/or C-reactive protein (CRP) ≥ 3.0 mg/dL, and prolonged PR interval (unless carditis is a major criterion).
  • Revised Jones criteria, moderate- and high-risk populations: Major and minor criteria are as follows:
    • Major criteria: Carditis (clinical and/or subclinical), arthritis (monopoly arthritis or polyarthritis, or polyarthralgia), chorea, erythema marginatum, and subcutaneous nodules
    • Minor criteria: fever (≥ 38.5° F), sedimentation rate ≥ 30 mm and/or CRP ≥ 3.0 mg/dL, and prolonged PR interval (unless carditis is a major criterion)
  • Remaining options—Carditis, Migratory polyarthritis and Erythema marginatum are Jones major criteria.

• The most appropriate position to relieve difficulty in breathing is Fowler's position.
  • Fowler's position is a standard patient position in which the patient is seated in a semi-upright sitting position and may have knees either bent or straight. There are several types of Fowler's positions: Low, Semi, Standard and High Fowler's. Low Fowler's position is when the head of bed is elevated 15 - 30 degrees, Semi-Fowler's position is 30 - 45 degrees, Standard Fowler's is 45 - 60 degrees, and High Fowler's position is 60 - 90 degrees. It is an intervention used to promote oxygenation via maximum chest expansion. It is an intervention used to promote oxygenation via maximum chest expansion, facilitates the relaxing of tension of the abdominal muscles, allowing for improved breathing and alleviates compression of the chest that occurs due to gravity. Hence this position is implemented during events of respiratory distress.
  • The dorsal recumbent position is a position in which an individual (usually a patient) lies on their back with their knees bent up in an outward position while their feet are planted flat on the ground, a bed, table or resting platform allowing the pelvic area to be easily examined and observed and not suitable in breathing difficulty patients.
  • Sims position is usually used for rectal examination, treatments and enemas.
  • Lateral position is also provided in patients with breathing difficulty, but Fowlers position is found more effective than lateral position.

choices.title: Auditory system
choices.correct_explanation:
• The Medial geniculate bodies form a part of the auditory system. The medial geniculate nucleus (MG) consists of a group of sub nuclei that receive auditory input from the midbrain and hindbrain and project mainly to the auditory cortex. Information travels from the receptors in the organ of Corti of the inner ear (cochlear hair cells) to the central nervous system, which is carried by the auditory nerve or vestibulocochlear nerve (CN VIII). This pathway is short, fast with large myelinated fibers and has only 3 to 4 relays and it ends in the primary auditory cortex.
  • The first relay of the primary auditory pathway occurs in the cochlear nuclei in the brainstem
  • The second major relay in the brainstem is in the superior olivary complex.
  • These two relays play an essential role in the localization of sound.
  • A last relay, before the cortex, occurs in the medial geniculate body (thalamus)
  • The primary auditory cortex is directly excited by the projections from the medial geniculate body.

Figure: Auditory pathway

  • Lateral geniculate body forms a part of visual pathway, which relays visual information from the optic tract to the visual cortex.
  • Limbic system constitutes hypothalamus, which is responsible for many of the behavioral functions.
  • Motor system called extrapyramidal motor system includes pathways through the basal ganglia, reticular formation of the brainstem, vestibular nuclei and the red nuclei.

Reference:

choices.correct_explanation:
• Profound hearing loss is described as greater than 80dB. Hearing loss, also known as hearing impairment, is a partial or total inability to hear. Hearing loss may occur in one or both ears and can be temporary or permanent. Human hearing extends in frequency from 20 - 20,000 Hz, and in intensity from 0 dB to 120 dB HL or more. The severity of a hearing loss is ranked according to range of nominal thresholds in which a sound must be heard so it can be detected by an individual. It is measured in decibels of hearing loss, or dB HL. Hearing loss may be ranked as slight, mild, moderate, moderately severe, severe or profound as defined in Table below:

Table: Degree of hearing

Degree of hearing

Decibels (dBs)

Explanation

Normal hearing

0 - 25 dB

Hearing is considered normal. However, people with 20 to 25 dB may have trouble hearing faint speech.

Mild hearing loss

26 - 40 dB

People with mild hearing loss might find it difficult keeping up with conversations, especially in noisy environments. They can usually hear well when talking to someone one-on-one but might struggle to hear distant speech

Moderate hearing loss

41 - 70 dB

They have difficulty hearing what’s being said when background noise is present. People with moderate hearing loss may request conversations be repeated as they can miss up to 75% of what was said.

Severe hearing loss

71 - 90 dB

People who have severe hearing loss will struggle to hear even loud speech. They may still be able to identify noises in the environment.

Profound deafness

90 dB+

People with profound hearing loss are considered deaf. It’s difficult for them to hear and understand sounds, even when amplified. They are usually aware of vibrations and predominantly rely on their other senses to interpret the world around them.
  • Other given options, i.e. 20 dB, 60 dB and 40 dB are incorrect.
